one_liner: Team messaging and collaboration suite with a rich open API platform.

evidence.claim: Lark Open Platform APIs are RESTful
evidence.quote: The APIs provided by Lark Open Platform follow the RESTful style

evidence.claim: APIs are authenticated via access tokens sent in the HTTP header; tenant_access_token lets an app call APIs without user authorization
evidence.quote: When calling the API, the access token needs to be filled in the HTTP request header.

evidence.claim: OAuth2-style user authorization flow with authorization code exists for user_access_token
evidence.quote: This API is used to initiate user authorization. After the user consents to the authorization, the application will receive an authorization code

evidence.claim: Developers self-serve by creating a custom app in the Developer Console to obtain App ID and App Secret credentials
evidence.quote: you can query the application credentials, that is, App ID and App Secret

evidence.claim: An official MCP server from Lark (larksuite/lark-openapi-mcp) wraps the OpenAPI as MCP tools
evidence.quote: This is the Feishu/Lark official OpenAPI MCP (Model Context Protocol) tool designed to help users quickly connect to the Feishu/Lark platform

notes: Official MCP server runs via npx (@larksuiteoapi/lark-mcp) using app_id/app_secret, supports tenant_access_token and user_access_token, stdio/SSE/streamable modes, and a beta --oauth flag. Three token types exist (tenant_, user_, app_access_token); app_access_token is being phased into tenant_access_token. Frictions: API scopes must be applied for per-endpoint; sensitive data permissions (e.g., Contacts, HR) require review; store apps require ISV qualification; production release of custom apps needs admin approval, though the test-tenant beta version takes effect 'without administrator review'.
